items.title: August Lanoix Interview, 1961-04-19
items.q: By being in this military band... There was a boy in there. His name is Gus Eli Show. He's on that picture.

ctx.x: One of the best ones I had. It was a Holden. You know if Professor Humphrey recommended a big bell or a little bell, did he ever talk anything about that? No. I've read there's quite a difference supposedly in the tongue, whether it's a big bell or a little bell. Just wondered if anybody paid any attention to that here. No. When did you take up the bakes? How did you happen to change?

I'll tell you how I happened to change on the bakes. By being in this military band, they had two other fellas which you see on there with trombones. And me, I made the fourth one I believe. They didn't select one of those men on there. There was a boy in there. His name is Gus Eli Show. He's on that picture. He wanted to form an orchestra, which he did. What we used to rehearse all the time was the three trombones. So they said that that was too many trombones for about a ten piece band. They only had two…

items.title: August Lanoix Interview, 1961-04-19
items.q: So that's when we got this, went on with this trio. ... And we used to play an orchestration with those three pieces from top to bottom.

ctx.x: Oh yeah. Gus Eli Show. Oh yeah. Well, he never did. The only band he ever played in was this. Big military. Military band there. So that's when we got this, went on with this trio. And we did very well. We used to play music. Take orchestration and give him the banjo part. My brother and I would take the clarinet. And we used to play an orchestration with those three pieces from top to bottom. Is that right, Clarence? Yeah. That's really right. Oh, wow. And when Three Little Boys came out, we were playing in a…

Well, there's one thing I forgot to ask about Professor Humphrey's lessons. Did he ever let you work on any of the little popular tunes, any of those late numbers that came out? Did he ever give you anything like that? Well, yeah.
